title: Cross-region fallthrough handoff: eu->us-west routing surge (2026-11-15)
content:
Summary:

Brief: During the 02:00–03:20 UTC watch we observed a sustained increase in 99th percentile latency for the hosted-api in the EU region which caused our smart-routing policy to begin fallthrough routing to US-WEST model pools. The routing fallthrough amplified tail latency and caused a transient spike in request queueing at the US-WEST ingress. This doc is the on-call handoff with timeline, mitigations, and follow-ups for the next shift.

Impact:
- Affected surface: hosted inference API endpoints (text-generation/chat) for eu region customers.
- User-visible symptoms: slow responses (5–30s) at p95/p99; small number (~0.6%) of requests hit model error retries and returned 503.
- Business impact: elevated error rate for a subset of low-latency customers, minor CS escalations from two customers using dedicated-reserved routing. No SLA breach confirmed yet; investigating error windows.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-11-15 01:58: alert triggered: eu-hosted-api p99 latency > 2.5s (Grafana alert).
- 02:02: paging to SRE on-call (Marcus) and serving-runtime on-call (Tomás).
- 02:05–02:10: verified increased tail latency correlating with a surge in long-request sequences (average sequence length +40% vs baseline).
- 02:12: routing autoswitch began: policy fallthrough threshold reached -> requests routed to compatible us-west pool.
- 02:15: observed queue length increase at us-west ingress; p99 in us-west rose.
- 02:20: emergency mitigation: manual adjust of smart-routing weight to prefer eu-fallback-cache instead of cross-region fallthrough (Aisha).
- 02:25: partial improvement in eu p99; us-west queue normalized over next 10m.
- 02:40: detected several 503s from a minority of requests due to model-serving retry cascades; mitigated by enabling temporary rate-limiter smoothing and increasing worker pool for dedicated customers (Tomás + infra automation).
- 03:05: monitoring shows metrics near baseline; alert resolved at 03:12.

Root cause hypothesis:
- Primary trigger: unexpected distribution shift — incoming requests had a higher-than-normal average sequence length and content complexity (longer prompt chains from a single client release in EU), increasing per-request token cost and effective inference time.
- Contributing factors:
  1) Smart-routing fallthrough threshold was too aggressive for short-duration bursts; it immediately routed traffic cross-region instead of using local cache/fallback variants.
  2) No short-circuit to apply local reduced-precision model variants (quantized) for bursty high-cost requests in eu-hosted-api.
  3) Rate-limiter smoothing not tuned for cross-region surge behavior, causing queueing in us-west ingress.

Actions taken (live):
- Short-term (incident window):
  - Lowered fallthrough weight and increased preference for local eu-fallback-cache chain (Aisha).
  - Temporarily enabled rate-limiter smoothing to throttle re-routed bursts (Tomás).
  - Added 15% worker oversell for dedicated eu pools to absorb queued requests (infra on-call).
  - Rolled forward a config that prefers quantized-compatible model variants for long sequence clients when cpu/GPU busy (hotfix PR referenced below).

Post-incident follow-ups (ownership assigned):
- SRE-1982 (Marcus): Tune smart-routing fallthrough thresholds to add a short holdback window (30–90s) before cross-region fallthrough for bursty latency patterns.
- INF-7420 (Lena): Add an automated fallback that first tries local quantized variant + prefix-KV cache before cross-region routing; ensure cost/quality telemetry captured.
- RUNBOOK-UPDATE (Aisha): Update eu-hosted-api runbook section "Cross-region fallthrough" with specific playbook steps we performed and new runbook commands to adjust routing weights.
- Telemetry (Tomás): Add a dashboard panel for sequence-length distribution by customer id and a synthetic test that simulates long prompt chains to eu region every 6 hours.
- Postmortem (assigned to Marcus + Lena): Capture customer IDs and request examples (sanitized) to validate model latency profile and work with model-onboarding if model variant mismatch contributed.

Runbook diffs / recommended edits (quick notes for next edit):
- Add explicit instruction: when p99 > 2.5s AND sequence-length-mean > baseline+30% -> do NOT immediately enable cross-region fallthrough; instead:
  1) Try local fallback variants (quantized) for 60s.
  2) If still > threshold, increase local worker pool by X% (configurable) and enable rate-limiter smoothing.
  3) As a last resort, enable cross-region fallthrough with throttling (cap at 10% of EU traffic).
- Add SLO guard: automated alert if cross-region routing > 5% for more than 10m.
- Add commands & links: grafana panels, routing weight quick-set CLI, and the hotfix PR link.

Outstanding operational tasks for next shift:
- Verify infra autoscaling logs for the time window; confirm oversell actions were honored and billing impact (Tomás) — due EOD.
- Run the synthetic long-prompt test, verify alerts silence and proper fallback invocation (Lena) — due next 24h.
- Draft postmortem doc with sanitized examples and timeline (Marcus) — draft by 2026-11-18.
- Update hosted-api customer-facing incident notes if postmortem determines customer-visible SLA risk (CS/ops coordination).

Notes for the next on-call person:
- Watch panels: eu-hosted-api p95/p99 latency, sequence-length distribution, cross-region-routing-rate, us-west ingress queue length. Links above.
- If alert re-triggers: first check sequence-length graph (spike indicates similar issue). If sequences are normal but latency high, investigate model-serving latency (GPU hot processes).
- CLI snippets: 
  - set-routing-weight --region eu --weight 0.9  (restore preference to eu)
  - enable-rate-smoothing --region us-west --window 60s --factor 0.5
  - scale-workers --pool eu-dedicated --delta +15%

Communication & escalation log (summary):
- Slack thread: #sre-eu-ops (link in linked_artifacts).
- Notified product/platform leads at 02:22; CS alerted at 02:35 for potential customer impact.
- No pager escalation to oncall-manager required; incident handled by primary on-call and infra.

Attachments / evidence indexes (in linked_artifacts):
- Grafana snapshot of latency + queue at peak.
- JIRA tickets created for tuning and postmortem.
- Hotfix PR: runtime routing weight control (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1347).

Closing note: The immediate mitigations restored baseline but uncovered missing guardrails for short-duration bursts with high sequence lengths. Primary priorities are (1) runbook insertion of the 60s local-fallback holdback, (2) telemetry for sequence-length by customer, and (3) a small automation to cap cross-region fallthrough to avoid amplification loops. Leaving the rest to the follow-ups above.

-- Aisha (eu overnight on-call)
